programme: A small chromatin-modifying module (ARID4B, TET1, KDM5D) re-activates a homeobox developmental gene set (HOXA5, HOXB3, plus HOXB5/HOXB6 which sit directly among ARID4B's own targets) that is normally silenced outside embryogenesis: ARID4B is a Rb-associated chromatin repressor that directly targets HOXB3/5/6 in this network, TET1 removes DNA methylation to permit gene reactivation, and KDM5D removes the repressive H3K4me3 mark at the same class of loci.
role_in_a: In lung cancer this chromatin/HOX module drives dedifferentiation and progression: ARID4B activates a GPRC5C-linked malignancy programme (41777148), TET1 acts as an epigenetic-remodeling tumor suppressor whose loss unlocks these same loci (40790761), KDM5D expression tracks clinicopathologic stage and survival (42323724), and HOXA5 has prognostic significance tied to progression pattern in small-cell lung cancer (42055886).
role_in_b: In multiple sclerosis the same machinery operates in glia rather than epithelium: TET1-dependent demethylation promotes oligodendrocyte generation and its dysregulation marks chronic inactive demyelinated lesions (39770028, 37286732); HOXA5 is induced as part of TGFB1-driven reactive gliosis in MS spinal cord (31779094) and its methylation state shifts in monocytes of primary progressive MS (37752647); HOXB3 rises in CSF and predicts conversion from clinically isolated syndrome to relapsing MS (33352356, 29873030), consistent with the same developmental-gene reactivation read out as a biomarker rather than a mechanism there.
shared_axis: Epithelial and glial lineages both keep an embryonic HOX programme locked down by DNA/histone methylation; when a tumor (lung) or a chronically damaged CNS region (MS) needs cells to leave a terminally differentiated state, the same demethylase/chromatin-repressor toolkit (TET1, KDM5D, ARID4B) is redeployed to reopen that HOX programme, producing dedifferentiated tumor cells in one tissue and dysmature reactive glia in the other.
reasoning: TET1 and HOXA5 are each independently documented with disease-relevant mechanism in both lung cancer and MS, and ARID4B's direct network targeting of HOXB3/5/6 gives a concrete topological link between the chromatin arm and the HOX arm — so the programme is nameable from the data itself, not asserted from silence. But KDM5D's MS evidence (37657612) is about its X-linked paralogs KDM5C/KDM6A, not KDM5D itself, and ARID4B/HOXB3 are each placed in only one of the two diseases by literature, so the cross-disease link rests partly on my construction of the module rather than on any retrieved statement connecting lung cancer and MS through it.
support: 41777148 (ARID4B drives lung adenocarcinoma malignancy); 42055886 (HOXA5 prognostic in lung SCLC progression); 37752647 (HOXA5-linked methylation shift in PPMS monocytes); 31779094 (HOXA5 induction in TGFB1-mediated MS gliosis); 40790761 (TET1 tumor-suppressor via epigenetic/immune remodeling in LUAD); 39770028 (TET1-dependent oligodendrocyte generation); 37286732 (TET1-era methylation changes in chronic demyelinated MS lesions); 33352356 and 29873030 (HOXB3 as CSF biomarker of CIS-to-MS conversion); 42323724 (KDM5D expression tied to lung carcinoma clinicopathology/survival); 37657612 (KDM5-family paralogs KDM5C/KDM6A, not KDM5D itself, regulate T-cell-driven autoimmunity — cited only as indirect family-level support, not direct KDM5D evidence).
how_to_falsify: Run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for ARID4B, TET1 and KDM5D in a lung adenocarcinoma line and in oligodendrocyte precursor cells or MS lesion-derived glia; if none of them occupies the HOXA5 or HOXB3 loci in either cell type, or if knocking down ARID4B fails to change HOXB3/HOXB5/HOXB6 expression despite the network's target call, and TET1/KDM5D knockdown leaves HOXA5/HOXB3 methylation and expression unchanged in both tissues, the shared chromatin-HOX axis is not real. Separately, testing KDM5D (not KDM5C) directly in a T-cell autoimmunity assay would confirm or remove the weakest link in the module.
caveats: Only 3 independent cohort pairs underlie the 728 patient-group comparisons, so the recurrence fractions are less independent than they look; ARID4B's 349/728 is the highest recurrence in the list but carries no multiple sclerosis literature evidence at all, and HOXB3's MS evidence is a CSF biomarker association rather than a mechanistic study. The tissue-generic exclusion list (NEUROD2, SOX2, TCF4, REST, EBF1, TAL1, DLX5 etc.) confirms that generic brain/lung identity factors were already stripped out, so the surviving module is not simply 'neural vs. epithelial master regulators' by default. Half the originally-listed factors (EBF2, DEAF1, TCFL5, and largely ARX, TBX3, MNX1, BACH1) had no evidence placing them in either disease or only in one, and were deliberately excluded from the programme rather than folded in to make the story more complete.
